Tenant.title: Tenant
Tenant.description: Represents a single business entity or store owner within the FreshTally multi-tenant application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tenant entity.

name.description: The legal or common name of the tenant's business.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the tenant record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the tenant record was last updated.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account associated with a specific tenant, used for role-based access control. Does not store authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity (typically the external authentication system's UID).

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant this user belongs to. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N User)

email.description: The user's email address, obtained from the authentication system.

displayName.description: The user's display name or full name.

role.description: The role of the user within the tenant (e.g., 'owner', 'staff').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user record was last updated.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a salable item managed by the inventory system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant who owns this product. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Product)

description.description: A brief description of the product.

price.description: The selling price of the product.

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) for the product, unique within a tenant.

imageUrl.description: URL to an image of the product.

isActive.description: Indicates if the product is currently active and available for sale.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the product record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the product record was last updated.

InventoryItem.title: InventoryItem
InventoryItem.description: Tracks the stock level and inventory details for a specific product within a tenant.

id.description: Unique identifier for the InventoryItem entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant who owns this inventory item. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N InventoryItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product this inventory item tracks. (Relationship: Product 1:1 InventoryItem)

stockLevel.description: The current quantity of the product in stock.

minStockLevel.description: The minimum stock level threshold to trigger a low-stock alert.

lastStockUpdate.description: Timestamp of the last update to the stock level.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the inventory item record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the inventory item record was last updated.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Represents a single point-of-sale transaction, capturing overall details of a sale.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant where this transaction occurred. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Transaction)

transactionDate.description: The date and time when the transaction was completed.

totalAmount.description: The total monetary amount of the transaction.

paymentMethod.description: The method used for payment (e.g., 'Cash', 'Credit Card', 'Debit Card').

status.description: The current status of the transaction (e.g., 'Completed', 'Pending', 'Refunded', 'Cancelled').

staffUserId.description: Reference to the User (staff member) who processed the transaction. (Relationship: User 1:N Transaction)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was last updated.

SaleItem.title: SaleItem
SaleItem.description: Represents a specific product included in a transaction, detailing quantity and price at the time of sale.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SaleItem entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant associated with the parent transaction. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N SaleItem)

transactionId.description: Reference to the Transaction this sale item belongs to. (Relationship: Transaction 1:N SaleItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product sold. (Relationship: Product 1:N SaleItem)

productName.description: Denormalized name of the product at the time of sale.

quantity.description: The quantity of the product sold.

unitPrice.description: The unit price of the product at the time of sale.

subtotal.description: The calculated subtotal for this item (quantity * unitPrice).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the sale item record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the sale item record was last updated.

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Records a business expense, potentially with AI-categorization.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant who incurred this expense. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Expense)

description.description: A detailed description of the expense.

amount.description: The monetary amount of the expense.

expenseDate.description: The date when the expense was incurred.

receiptUrl.description: URL to a digital copy of the receipt for the expense.

notes.description: Additional notes or details about the expense.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was last updated.

definition.description: Root collection for each business tenant. Documents here store tenant-specific metadata. Accessible by users who are 'owner' for the specific tenantId. Includes denormalized 'ownerId' or relies on 'users' collection for authorization.

Top-level collection for all user profiles. Each document represents a user account and contains their 'tenantId' and 'role'. This structure is CRITICAL for Authorization Independence, enabling security rules to quickly ascertain a user's tenancy and permissions without additional 'get()' calls to other tenant-scoped collections.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure addresses the reported 'Missing or insufficient permissions' error by implementing strict multi-tenancy rules and adhering to the core design principles, especially 'Authorization Independence' and 'QAPs (Rules are not Filters)'. The primary strategy is to use a top-level `users/{userId}` collection to store each user's `tenantId` and `role`. This critical denormalization allows security rules to retrieve the current user's authorization context (their associated tenant and role) with a single, performant `get()` operation on their own user document, rather than requiring multiple `get()` calls across different tenant documents or subcollections.

All tenant-specific data (Products, Inventory, Transactions, Sale Items, Expenses) are organized as subcollections under `/tenants/{tenantId}/`. This structural segregation ensures that data for different tenants is physically separated and that all documents within a given subcollection share the same security posture – they all belong to the same tenant and require authorization based on that tenant's rules. For instance, `/tenants/{tenantId}/transactions` clearly indicates that all documents here are transactions for `{tenantId}`.

Authorization Independence is achieved because the `tenantId` is present in the document path (`/tenants/{tenantId}/...`) and the user's `tenantId` and `role` are directly available from their `/users/{userId}` document. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls to parent documents within specific collection rules, making rules atomic and easier to debug. For the error specifically, a rule for `/tenants/{tenantId}/transactions` would check `request.auth.uid` against the `userId` in `users/{userId}` to retrieve their `tenantId` and `role`. Then, it would assert that the `tenantId` from the path matches the user's assigned `tenantId` and that their `role` grants permission for the 'list' operation. This design enables a direct and explicit authorization check.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters) are supported by ensuring that the `tenantId` in the path (`{tenantId}`) is always explicitly validated against the authenticated user's `tenantId` (obtained from their `/users/{userId}` document). When a client attempts to 'list' documents from `/tenants/33353/transactions`, the rule will check if `request.auth.uid` belongs to tenant '33353' and has the necessary role. If the user's `tenantId` (from their user profile) does not match '33353', or if they lack the appropriate role, the `list` operation will be denied *before* any documents are returned, satisfying QAPs. This prevents partial data returns due to security rules and ensures that all data retrieved by a query is fully authorized, simplifying client-side logic and enhancing security.
